skill_name: Client-Side Data Fetching, Offline Storage & Security
subtopic: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Prevention and Content Security Policy (CSP)
question_text: [Client-Side Data Fetching, Offline Storage & Security - Q55] How does a robust Content Security Policy (CSP) with `script-src 'nonce-...';` mitigate Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)?

options.text: It encrypts all JavaScript files on the server
It instructs the browser to refuse execution of any inline `<script>` or external script tag that does not possess the cryptographic per-request nonce
It disables all REST API calls made with fetch()
It sanitizes SQL queries executed in WebSQL

answer_explanation: Attackers injecting arbitrary `<script>evil()</script>` cannot predict the server-generated cryptographic nonce, so the browser unconditionally blocks execution.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: Attackers injecting arbitrary `<script>evil()</script>` cannot predict the server-generated cryptographic nonce, so the browser unconditionally blocks execution.
